data.description:
## Problem
The reconciler multi-project fan-out (story 1734) runs every mapped project's base
(active + done-recent) JQL queries in a single flat loop with NO per-project error
isolation: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot` builds
`queries` across all projects and iterates `for jql, cap in queries:` — any single
project's transport failure (ACLI 400 unknown-project, 401/403 permission, 404,
429 rate-limit, 5xx, timeout) propagates out and ABORTS THE ENTIRE PASS for all
projects. The enrichment loop directly below already fails open per-project
(`_enrich_project` "each pass failing open independently so a per-project fault
degrades only that project"). The base-query loop never inherited that resilience.

This is the PROVEN root cause of the 2026-08-15 production outage (bug
05b8-4efe-8d58-4c27): a single mapped-but-nonexistent project key (`LEG`) —
syntactically valid, so `_validate_project_key` passes — made ACLI exit 1 and took
down ~12h of scheduled Reconcile Bridge passes across every project.

## Approach
Wrap each project's base-query fetch in a per-project boundary that mirrors the
enrichment loop's fail-open contract: on a per-project transport error, SKIP that
project (do not merge partial results that would look like deletions), emit an
observable alert via `alert_store.append({"kind": "fetcher-project-fetch-failed",
"project": <key>, "pass_id": pass_id, ...})`, mark the pass degraded, and CONTINUE
to the other projects. Preserve the existing fail-CLOSED behavior for a
syntactically-invalid/absent key (that still raises in `jql_active` — bug 626d
intent is unchanged) and for a `BackendPaginationStallError` (a stalled pager is a
truncated whole-project read and must still surface), matching the enrichment
loop's exception handling exactly.

## Acceptance criteria
1. One mapped project's base-query transport error does not abort the pass; other
   projects' issues still land in the snapshot.
2. A per-project fetch failure emits an observable alert naming the project + pass.
3. The single-project (unseeded store) path remains regression-identical.
4. Syntactically-invalid/absent key still fails closed (626d preserved); a
   pagination-stall still re-raises.

## Test plan (always-on unit — closes the P0-3 test gap)
Add a unit to `tests/.../test_fetch_multi_project.py` using a `_FakeClient` whose
`search_issues` RAISES for project `BAD` (e.g. HTTPError 400) but returns issues
for `GOOD`; assert GOOD's issues land, the pass is not aborted, and the per-project
alert fired. This is the always-on (no live Jira) regression the incident lacked.
Add mutation check: reverting the per-project try/except returns the test to RED.

## Sequencing
Edits `fetcher.py` `_build_snapshot` base-query region. Ticket C (non-Done status)
also edits `fetcher.py` — C is sequenced AFTER this ticket to avoid conflict.
data.title: Reconciler fan-out: per-project resilience in base-query loop (no whole-pass abort on one bad project)
